commits.message:
Add Copilot Issue Triage agentic workflow (POC) (#22342)

* Add Copilot Issue Triage agentic workflow (POC)

Adds a scheduled GitHub Agentic Workflow (gh-aw) that finds well-scoped,
maintainer-approved issues and assigns them to the GitHub Copilot coding
agent for a fix PR. Adapted from github/gh-aw issue-monster.

- copilot-issue-triage.md: gh-aw source workflow (edit + `gh aw compile`)
- copilot-issue-triage.lock.yml: compiled Actions workflow (generated)
- .github/aw/actions-lock.json: pinned action versions (gh-aw scaffolding)
- .gitattributes: mark *.lock.yml as linguist-generated / merge=ours

Safety: the agent job is read-only; all writes go through safe-outputs.
Assignment is gated on an opt-in `copilot-candidate` label, restricted to
the copilot agent, capped at 2/run. A deterministic pre-activation search
scopes candidates via a single per-team CONFIG block (shipped for the RM
team: Area: Release / Area:RM / Tasks owned by @manolerazvan in CODEOWNERS).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Use per-team gate label; RM team uses copilot-candidate-rm

Set CONFIG.gateLabel to a team-specific value so multiple teams sharing
this workflow do not process the same issue via a shared label. RM now
gates on `copilot-candidate-rm`. All agent/human-facing text is made
label-agnostic (the literal label lives only in CONFIG.gateLabel), so a
forking team edits only the CONFIG block.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Rework triage into nomination->approval handshake

Invert the single gate label into a two-label handshake so a maintainer
always has the final say before Copilot is engaged:

* copilot-candidate-rm (nomination) is bot-applied; copilot-approved-rm
  (approval) is applied manually by a maintainer and only read by the
  workflow.
* Per run: CONFIRM issues carrying both labels (assign to Copilot,
  comment, remove nomination label); throttle new nominations while any
  issue is nominated-but-unapproved; otherwise scan the open/unassigned
  in-scope pool, score, and nominate the top N (default 2).
* Add an issues.labeled trigger for instant confirmation the moment a
  maintainer adds the approval label; no-ops for any other label.
* CONFIG gains nominationLabel/approvalLabel/nominateCount; safe-outputs
  gain add-labels/remove-labels (nomination label only) and a higher
  add-comment cap. Pre-activation outputs and the agent gate updated to
  the new confirm/nominate model. Recompiled lock.yml (0 errors/0 warnings).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Skip confirmation when issue is already assigned

Addresses PR review feedback: the instant issues.labeled confirmation
path could assign Copilot to an issue that already has an assignee,
clobbering a manual assignment. Now the fast path skips an approved
issue that already has assignees, and the scheduled CONFIRM search adds
no:assignee for parity. Recompiled lock.yml (0 errors/0 warnings).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Grant least-privilege read scopes to pre-activation job

Addresses PR review feedback: with top-level permissions: {} and no
job-level permissions, the pre_activation job's GITHUB_TOKEN had no
scopes, so searching issues, reading CODEOWNERS, enriching linked PRs,
and the role check would fail at runtime. Add on.permissions
(contents/issues/pull-requests: read) — the gh-aw field that scopes the
pre-activation on.steps job — separate from the agent job's own
permissions. Recompiled lock.yml (0 errors/0 warnings).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address PR review: deterministic Copilot assignment + hardening

Move Copilot assignment out of the AI agent and into the deterministic
pre-activation step, enforcing the human-approval gate in the system
rather than the prompt (review comment #398). The agent's only capability
is now NOMINATION (add candidate label + comment); it has no assign or
remove-label tool, so a crafted/injected issue body cannot bypass approval.

- Assign approved+unassigned issues to the Copilot coding agent via GraphQL
  replaceActorsForAssignable in the pre-activation github-script; then remove
  the nomination label and post a transparency comment. Requires issues:write.
- Remove assign-to-agent and remove-labels from safe-outputs; drop confirm_*
  job outputs; rewrite the NL body to nomination-only.
- Nomination comment now spells out the exact next steps that happen after a
  maintainer approves (assign, label cleanup, draft PR, human review).
- Hardening from the same review: empty Task-name field parsed by a line-based
  reader (147); exact Copilot bot-author allowlist instead of includes copilot
  (322); paginate linked-PR cross-references up to 500 (258); paginate the
  nomination pool search and warn on truncation (281); use listForRepo
  (read-after-write consistent, fully paged) for confirm/pending sets (297).
- Update POC header, CONFIG comments, and the local dryrun.js harness for
  parity. Recompiles 0 errors / 0 warnings.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.message:
Split Copilot Issue Triage into nominate + approved-processing workflows (POC) (#22343)

* Split Copilot issue triage into nominate + approved-processing workflows

Splits the single copilot-issue-triage workflow into two, so nomination
and post-approval processing are independent and each has a clear trigger.

Why: assigning the GitHub Copilot coding agent is not permitted with the
Actions GITHUB_TOKEN (a GitHub App installation token returns "Assigning
agents is not supported..."). Only a human/user token can assign the agent.
So the workflow can never assign Copilot itself. This split makes the flow
match that reality:

- copilot-issue-triage (gh-aw, schedule + workflow_dispatch): NOMINATION only.
  A read-only pre-activation search builds a scored candidate pool; the agent
  adds one nomination label (copilot-candidate-rm) and a comment explaining
  that a maintainer approves by ASSIGNING Copilot. Removed: the approval label,
  the issues:labeled trigger, the deterministic Copilot-assignment code
  (getCopilotActorId/confirmIssue/replaceActorsForAssignable) and the instant
  confirm fast-path. Pre-activation permissions dropped to issues:read.
  Nomination is throttled while any nominated issue is still unassigned.

- copilot-issue-triage-approved (plain Actions, issues:assigned +
  workflow_dispatch): POST-APPROVAL housekeeping. When a maintainer manually
  assigns the Copilot coding agent (the approval), it removes the nomination
  label, adds a copilot-working label, and comments. Deterministic label/comment
  bookkeeping keyed on the assignee, so no LLM and nothing to compile. It does
  not (and cannot) assign Copilot. Every assigned event proceeds to a live
  assignees check + copilot-working idempotency guard, so housekeeping is not
  dropped if a pending run is canceled by a newer assignment.

POC note to validate at runtime: confirm assigning the Copilot agent fires
issues.assigned with login copilot-swe-agent/copilot (both are matched).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Address PR #22343 review: clearer concurrency comment, fail-fast label ordering, assignee wording

- approved.yml: rewrite the "don't decide off the triggering assignee" comment
  to explain the real reason (stale/partial webhook payload), not the
  concurrency cancel edge case, which was misleading.
- approved.yml: add the copilot-working guard label FIRST and fail fast if it
  cannot be added, then remove the nomination label, then comment. Prevents an
  issue ending up with neither label and a re-run re-commenting; the comment's
  note now reflects whether the nomination removal actually succeeded.
- copilot-issue-triage.md: note in the nomination comment that the Copilot
  assignee may appear as copilot-swe-agent in the Assignees picker.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.message:
Top up Copilot nomination pool to N outstanding candidates (#22358)

Replace the all-or-nothing nomination throttle with a top-up model. Add
CONFIG.targetCandidateCount (N=2) to the RM config: the number of
OUTSTANDING candidates (nominated but still unassigned) to keep
available for maintainers. Each scheduled run now counts outstanding
candidates and, if fewer than N, nominates enough NEW issues to refill
the pool back up to N (bounded by the existing per-run cap
nominateCount). Previously any single outstanding nomination blocked all
new nominations, so the pool could sit at 1 (or drop toward 0 as
maintainers approved) until it fully cleared.

The number nominated this run flows to the agent via the nominate_count
output (= min(nominateCount, N - pending)); the agent still picks the
best topic-separated issues from the scored pool, up to that count.

Regenerated copilot-issue-triage.lock.yml via gh aw compile (0 err/0 warn).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
